Commentary.Commentary: A win will definitely put India in pole position to qualify for the Super Fours, but just for the math, they will not get a Q tonight officially. Strutting their fearless approach, won't put it past them to chase this score in a canter, but a couple of quick wickets might just put a simmer of a doubt in their minds. The Indian openers are ready to get back to the middle - Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill. It will be Shaheen Afridi to start things off with the ball. Abhishek to face. Wow. In that entire innings, barely remember seeing Gill on the field! Anyway, here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, it’s over to India’s batters. With 128 runs needed in 120 balls, the target looks light, but Pakistan’s new-ball pair will come hard, hoping for early breakthroughs. Can India crush this chase in the first six overs, or will Pakistan’s bowlers conjure an unlikely twist? Also, seven of the last eight India-Pakistan T20Is have been won by the team batting second, which tilts heavily in India's favour, but let's see how it goes. The chase is about to begin, so don't go anywhere.

Kuldeep Yadav’s golden spell sealed Pakistan’s collapse. The wrist-spinner claimed Hasan Nawaz and Mohammad Nawaz off back-to-back deliveries, before removing a defiant Farhan. Varun Chakaravarthy joined the party, trapping Faheem LBW, leaving Pakistan tottering at 97/8 by the 18th over. Bumrah then cleaned up Muqeem after a brief cameo of 10, reducing Pakistan to near submission. But Afridi’s fearless hitting at the death, at a 206.25 strike rate including four towering sixes, dragged them to 127/9, a score that looked impossible just three overs earlier.

The middle overs were where India’s spinners turned the screw. Axar Patel struck with Fakhar’s wicket, before trapping skipper Salman Agha for a scratchy inning. The runs dried up, the dot balls piled, and Pakistan’s frustration showed. At 49/4 in 10 overs, India were in complete control, with the surface offering slow turn and grip exactly as the bowlers had hoped. Pakistan’s batting looked sluggish and unsettled, unable to counter the relentless spin assault. Of the combined 13 overs bowled across four spinners used, they conceded only 65 runs, picking up 6 wickets, at an economy of under 6 runs per over.

It all began with chaos. Salman Agha won the toss and chose to bat, but Pakistan’s innings derailed in the first eight balls. Saim Ayub fell for a golden duck to Hardik Pandya's first legal ball after a wide first ball, and in-form Mohammad Haris followed soon after, dismissed by Jasprit Bumrah. At 6/2, disaster was written on the wall. Fakhar Zaman had a lifeline, overturning an LBW against Bumrah when playing just his second delivery, but pressure remained thick. Still, along with Sahibzada Farhan, he dragged Pakistan to 42/2 at the end of the Powerplay.

TWO SIXES in the final over from Shaheen Afridi have lifted Pakistan past 120, but is 127 enough against India’s fiery batting lineup? That would remain the question. On paper, the answer might be a 'No,' yet cricket loves a surprise, and Pakistan will pray and hope that their bowlers can pull off something magical. For India, the target screams of opportunity to kill the game in the Powerplay, make use of the fielding restrictions, and take away every ounce of hope from their rivals.

Commentary.Commentary: 282 chased down with ease. With 8 wickets and 35 balls to spare. This is an update from the 1st match of a 3-ODI series between India Women and Australia Women, in Mullanpur. After electing to bat first, half centuries from Pratika Rawal, Smriti Mandhana and Harleen Deol gave the home side a good start, but there was a lack of acceleration in the middle overs. India posted a decent enough total of 281/7, but had they been a bit more mobile post the 10th over, they might have got to 320. Australia made a literal mockery of the chase, with plenty of help from their counterparts as the Indians dropped catches left, right and centre, with special love for Phoebe Litchfield, who was allowed plenty of opportunities to get a century but fell short by 12 runs. Ellyse Perry retired hurt due to cramps but nearly all the batters got some decent batting practice. Earlier, Australia struggled to pick up wickets but managed to keep the Indians quiet.

Commentary.Commentary: The national anthems have been sung and we are ready for some cricketing action. The two openers for Pakistan - Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan - stride out to the middle. Hardik Pandya has the new ball in his hand. Ayub to face. Here we go.
The two squads walk out to the middle, for the national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by that of India's.

PITCH REPORT - Sanjay Manjrekar and Ravi Shastri are pitchside with their thoughts. Manjrekar points out that Pakistan’s decision to bat first seemed to have a lot to do with the nature of the surface. Ravi Shastri joins in and agrees. On the point of Pakistan going in with four spinners and just one specialist seamer, Shastri explains that Pakistan are going with a horses-for-courses approach. According to him, they believe that the track looks low and slow, and their idea is to play fearless cricket by putting runs on the board and then applying scoreboard pressure. Sanjay feels that this particular approach from Pakistan is a sign that they are completely revamping their strategy under Mike Hesson. Ravi adds that Pakistan’s spin options give them depth and flexibility, while India look like a very balanced side with all bases covered.

The Indian captain, Suryakumar Yadav, shares that they were looking to bowl, so he is happy with the toss result. Says that the preparations have been good and they are looking forward to this game. Highlights that they played their first game just one strip away and says it was a nice wicket overall and better to bat under the lights. Points that it is a bit humid, and hopes that the dew factor will come into play later. Informs that they are going unchanged for this game.

The skipper of Pakistan, Salman Agha, mentions that his team has been playing good cricket and the atmosphere is exciting. Talking about the surface, he feels that it looks like a slow wicket, so the plan is to bat first and put runs on the board. On the spin department, he confirms that they are going with the same side which played in the previous match. Speaking about playing in Dubai, he adds that the team has been here for around 20 days and is well used to the conditions.

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Sanju Samson (WK), Shivam Dube, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy, and Jasprit Bumrah.

Pakistan (Unchanged Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi, Sufiyan Muqeem, and Abrar Ahmed.
TOSS UPDATE - The coin flip lands in favor of Pakistan and Salman Agha elects to BAT first.

India's KULDEEP YADAV is up for a quick chat with the broadcasters. He reflects and expresses that he is happy with the way he performed in the previous game and cites the importance of starting off on a positive note. Shares that it is always tough to sit out for many games but mentions it is purely because of the conditions and the demands of the team at the very point. Highlights that he has worked on his fitness and bowled around 35 overs in the recently concluded Duleep Trophy. Mentions that the conditions in Dubai tend to get a bit slow as the game progresses. About the nerves during an India-Pakistan game, he adds that it is just another game of cricket. Says every player in the side wants to do well because of the history of both teams.

India and Pakistan have met three times in Dubai, in T20Is, with Pakistan winning twice, including that memorable ten-wicket victory at the 2021 T20 World Cup, and during the 2022 Asia Cup Super 4s. But overall, India still hold a strong record at the venue with six wins in ten outings in the format. Pakistan, on the other hand, have far greater experience in this regard, having played 33 matches, winning 18 of them, although their recent run has seen three defeats in the last five. With all said, let’s hope for quality cricket between the two nations. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

For Pakistan, the big question had been whether they could keep pace with the modern demands of T20 cricket, and lately they seem to have found some answers. Saim Ayub has quickly emerged as a pivotal figure for the future, while Salman Agha's leadership has added a proactive edge. The real challenge, though, is for this young batting unit to stand up against a high-quality Indian bowling attack. And when bowling quality is mentioned, Pakistan’s pace artillery always comes into focus. Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf have been lethal operators, especially with the new ball, and in the spin department, the trio of Mohammad Nawaz, Sufiyan Muqeem, and Abrar Ahmed will look to choke the opposition through the middle overs.

Staying true to their ultra-aggressive brand of cricket, India, under Suryakumar Yadav, are packed with power-hitters right through the order. The intent to go big from the very first ball is what makes this young side lethal. Abhishek Sharma showed flashes of that fearless approach in the previous outing, though the real test comes against stronger opposition like tonight. With the ball, the spinners led by Kuldeep Yadav enjoyed a productive day against the UAE, and similar conditions in Dubai suggest they could once again play a decisive role. India went in with just Jasprit Bumrah as the lone specialist quick, but Arshdeep Singh remains firmly in the frame. He has the second-best record for India among active players in the current squad, against Pakistan in terms of wickets, only behind Hardik Pandya, in T20Is. His inclusion, though, hinges on whether the team management is willing to sacrifice a batter to accommodate him.

The last time these two sides faced each other, India had the experience of Rohit Sharma, the aggression of Virat Kohli, and the electrifying presence of Ravindra Jadeja in the lineup. Pakistan’s batting card then was powered by their senior pros Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam. Now, none of them are part of their respective squads of this format. Some have retired, while others have been moved aside. With the greats gone, the focus has shifted to a new generation, a group carrying youthful energy, intensity, and the hunger to create their own legacy.

A lot has been happening and being talked off the field and on social media, as always has been the case when these two sides are about to clash. But on the field, it is simply about playing cricket like any other regular day or against any opposition. However, it’s the environment that is a bit somber this time around, as there was absolutely no certainty whether this would even be played in the first place. In the context of the tournament, it is an important clash for both sides. They started off with strong wins against lesser competitive opponents, and a win here will almost confirm the berth for the Super 4s. A defeat, however, will make the hill steeper moving forward.

Rivalries in cricket, or rather in any sport, make it a lot more lively and competitive. Years have gone by, but in any multilateral event, one of the most talked-about ones is India vs Pakistan. These two fierce sides go hard at each other, and when national pride is on the line, it becomes about unity and giving absolutely everything. Dubai is the hotspot and is all prepared for a Super Sunday. On that note, a warm welcome to our coverage.
... MATCH DAY ...

Rivalry, emotion, and a stage that needs no introduction. When India and Pakistan walk out to face each other, cricket becomes more than just a sport. The Asia Cup 2025 now delivers its biggest moment yet as Match 6 takes center stage in Dubai, with millions of voices ready to turn the stadium into a cauldron of noise and passion. History, politics, legacy, and controversy have long shaped this clash, but on the field, it all comes down to bat versus ball, nerve versus nerve. The most important Group A contest is here, and the world will be watching. For weeks, the biggest question wasn’t about who might win, but whether this clash would even happen at all. Now that uncertainty has been put to bed, the stage is finally clear for a blockbuster. Off the field, the rivalry often feels like life or death - pun intended - but on the field, it’s simply cricket in its most electrifying form. And with India and Pakistan meeting only in multilateral events, every contest feels like a rare gem. Both sides have warmed up with convincing wins over associate nations, brushing aside early hurdles and storming into Dubai with momentum on their side. The Men in Blue made light work of UAE, putting on a commanding display across every department. In fact, the contest barely stretched past the halfway mark, lasting under 20 overs in total, such was the gulf in quality. Dubai’s pitch has already shown its true colors, with spin calling the shots. In the opening match here, India’s spinners combined to take six of the eleven wickets that fell across both innings, with Kuldeep Yadav leading the way. Pakistan’s clash with debutants Oman followed the same script, as their spinners shared nine of the seventeen wickets across both innings, including a run out, and with Ayub and Muqeem at the forefront. One key difference stands out. Pakistan’s batting unit has already faced a proper test, while India’s middle order is still waiting for its first real challenge. How that balance tips in Dubai could well shape the story of this contest. The last time India and Pakistan met in the Asia Cup’s T20I format was back in 2022, where Pakistan got the better of the Indian side. Additionally, on the international stage, their last meet was more than a year ago, at the T20 World Cup 2024 in New York. That night had every bit of drama, as India defended just 119 runs against a full-strength Pakistani side. Since then, the landscape has shifted. Pakistan seem to have finally moved on from Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam from the format, who once used to be the very pillars of the side. India too has seen its greats bid farewell, with Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja hanging up their boots after lifting the trophy in that very tournament. What remains are two teams in a transition phase, reshaped with new faces, combinations, and fresh ambitions. And now, they are about to be thrown straight into the furnace of the highest intensity. Batting in unforgiving warm and humid conditions on slow, low pitches will be a real test for both sides. For many players, this will be their very first time facing the opposition in a contest of such magnitude. Yet there are a few who know exactly what it means to deliver on this stage. Picture Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf charging in full tilt at Shubman Gill and Suryakumar Yadav, or Jasprit Bumrah and Kuldeep Yadav taking on Salman Agha and Mohammad Haris. These are the duels within the duel, the battles that can decide the outcome. Both teams are moving forward on the lines of being more receptive to the demands of modern-day T20 cricket. Power-hitting depth, leaning more toward youth energy, coupled with flexible batting orders and multi-skilled players, is slowly becoming the blueprint of the way forward in the future. India and Pakistan may be in transition, but their approaches show a clear intent to keep pace with the evolving game. One thing is certain - in the current climate, every action and every reaction will be viewed through a magnifying glass. The atmosphere may feel a touch somber this time, but the hope remains that cricket itself does not get overshadowed. A fascinating night lies ahead, with the iconic Dubai International Cricket Stadium ready to sparkle under the spotlight.
